svg.title: nnAccelerator architecture — corner-fed, anti-diagonal output
svg.desc: RTL architecture at N=3. A one-entry vector register feeds shared registered row skew chains. Left taps enter all rows; right taps enter rows one and two. Top-left PEs move activations right and partial sums down; bottom-right PEs move activations left and partial sums up. Anti-diagonal PEs w02, w11, w20 take their own activation from the left and merge upper and lower sums in their existing MAC registers. Their three results connect directly to activation, with no output alignment registers. Host weight rows are collected bottom-first into an N by N bank and shifted into the top and bottom column chains before simultaneous capture. Activation and weighted reduction feed a result FIFO containing the activated vector, prediction and reduction signs. A separate sample-context FIFO contains the target, original input signs and training enable. Both heads retire together. Error and update directions feed both array corners, N minus one matrix update delay stages, and an N-stage reduction update pipe connected to the resident reduction weights. Ready/valid backpressure holds computation and learning together.
svg.text: Parallel ready/valid interface · one clock domain · default N = 3
Collect N host rows, then N shifts + capture
N × N PE array · resident W
LOAD: AD lower sum gated; bottom[0] unused
existing AD MAC registers · no alignment stage
W update delay pipe · N−1 stages
a[N] · applied once, after AD registers
same W package → live at both corners
result full + no pop → hold MAC/skew
TL: right/down BR: left/up AD: local product + both sums; activation supplied from left
N=3: accept → result FIFO 5 edges → earliest retire 6. Row 0 has no right injection.
Grey-green: storage/control; dashed top/bottom feeds = loading
Crossovers have no dot; dots mark connections.
